content.what_it_is: MATLAB spectrum converter that loads and transposes FRF spectral density data, constructs frequency/direction coordinates and marginal spectra, and plots the raw spectrum (L3-L62); it centers a bounded submatrix on the global peak, plots truncated spectra and random phase (L66-L129), converts density to component amplitudes, and writes separate 2-D and 1-D FUNWAVE-style spectrum files (L131-L168).
entities: script workspace cleared by clear all @L1

maximum direction from column count and spacing
root-mean-square height derived from integrated energy
frequency truncation window centered on peak
direction truncation window centered on peak

io.name: fprintf 2-D header, period, frequencies, and directions
fprintf 1-D header, period, frequencies, and direction

unresolved: The centered truncation formulas are inclusive at both ends: with an interior peak and even NFreq=50 or NDir=30 (L69-L72), L73-L74 select 51 or 31 indices respectively, exceeding the variables named as maxima by one.

Peak ties are not reduced to one location: find at L68 can return vector peakf/peakd, while colon ranges at L73-L74 require scalar endpoints; tied global maxima can therefore make truncation fail or become ambiguous (L67-L74).

The truncated frequency subplot plots x=Amp_Frq_model and y=Freq_model at L93, but L94-L95 label the y-axis as spectral density and x-axis as frequency, the reverse of both the plotted arguments and the corresponding raw subplot labels at L35-L37.

The displayed phase is generated as Phase at L86 and plotted at L119, but the phase written to wave2d_frf.txt is independently regenerated as Phase_input at L137 and appended at L151; the phase panel therefore does not depict the output realization (L86, L119, L137, L151).

The 2-D amplitude is explicitly transposed to direction-by-frequency layout at L133-L136 before writing at L150, whereas the 1-D amplitude derived as a frequency-column vector at L159 is not transposed before L166 even though L162 declares NumDir=1; whether the consumer reads a flat stream or requires the same NumDir-by-NumFreq row layout is unresolved (L133-L136, L150, L159, L162, L166).
angle_end is assigned at L12 but never referenced through EOF L170; thmax instead derives solely from NumDir at L17, so changing angle_end has no effect on the direction grid (L12, L17-L19).

Each output remains open through fid after fprintf (L145-L149 and L161-L165) while dlmwrite separately appends to the same pathname before fclose (L150-L153 and L166-L168); ordering and buffering behavior for the two simultaneous file access paths is not established in this file.
